How to remove AI traces from documents and emails you polished with ChatGPT or Copilot

You used ChatGPT or Copilot to polish a report, a cover letter or an email. Before you send it, check the technical traces the file carries — they can say more than the text itself.

Updated 2026-11-07 · 6 min read
Clean your files in secondsFree, no sign-up, and everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Open IA Cleaner

1. Document metadata (Word, PowerPoint, Excel)

Every .docx, .pptx and .xlsx is a package that includes hidden properties:

  • Author and Last modified by — the account names that created and edited the file.
  • Company, Manager and the Template the document was based on.
  • Application and version, plus total editing time.
  • Custom properties added by add-ins, templates, online tools or your organisation (for example classification labels).

If you started from a document generated or exported by an online AI tool, its name can remain in these fields even after you rewrite every line.

2. PDF properties

A PDF stores Creator (the app that made the original) and Producer (the PDF engine), plus an XMP block. PDFs exported from AI writing or presentation tools often carry that tool’s name there. See the full PDF metadata guide.

3. AI images inside the document

An illustration you generated with ChatGPT, DALL·E, Firefly or Midjourney and pasted into a slide keeps its own metadata — C2PA Content Credentials and XMP fields such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia — inside the .pptx or .docx. Anyone can unzip the file and read it.

4. Copy-paste leftovers in the text

  • Invisible characters: zero-width spaces, word joiners, special no-break spaces.
  • Citation markers such as contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0} or 【4:0†source】.
  • Links ending in ?utm_source=chatgpt.com — the recipient sees it when hovering or clicking.

More details in ChatGPT hidden characters.

5. Emails: what travels with your message

When you paste from a chat into Gmail or Outlook, you also paste its hidden characters, tracking parameters and sometimes HTML formatting (fonts, background colours). Attachments carry all the metadata above.

  1. Clean the text in IA Cleaner → Text and copy the result.
  2. Paste it into your email as plain text: Ctrl+Shift+V (⌘+Shift+V on Mac).
  3. Clean any attachment in Documents before attaching it.

How to clean a document with IA Cleaner

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Documents and drop your .docx, .pptx, .xlsx or PDF.
  2. Keep both options on: clean images embedded in documents and remove invisible characters from document text.
  3. Review the report — author, company, application, custom properties and embedded images are listed, AI-related ones are flagged.
  4. Download the clean copy. Your text, layout and images are unchanged; only the hidden data is removed.

Other ways

  • Word / PowerPoint on Windows: File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document → Document Properties and Personal Information → Remove All.
  • Word on Mac: Word → Preferences → Security → Remove personal information from this file on save.

These built-in tools don’t clean images embedded in the document or hidden characters in the text.

Checklist before you send

  • Text pasted as plain text, with no oaicite markers or utm_source=chatgpt.com links.
  • Document properties empty or correct (author, company, application).
  • Embedded images cleaned.
  • PDF exported after cleaning the original, or cleaned itself.

IA Cleaner removes technical traces; it doesn’t change your wording.
